results.title: Playback User Guide
results.summary: The master user guide. Relevant documented points: the Audio Device setting (Settings > General > Audio Device) chooses the device Playback uses for all audio output; Auto Pan sends click/guide left and tracks right on the headphone output; MultiOuts (Premium) allow up to 32 outputs; track routing lives in Settings > Tracks and bus routing in Settings > Buses; purchased tracks download free; downloaded setlists stay on the device until removed or until a different user signs in; Settings > About has Manage Subscription and Restore Purchases.

steps.text: Select the output device: tap the stack icon (top-right) > Settings > General > Audio Device.

Auto Pan: Settings > General > Auto-Pan. Sends click and guide to the left output and all tracks to the right output of the device's stereo output, so you can run tracks from the headphone port without an interface.
Track routing: Settings > Tracks, tap an instrument part and choose a bus. Routing is device-specific and applies to that track across all songs and setlists on that device.
Bus routing: Settings > Buses, tap a bus cell, choose an output, tap Done. Swipe left on a bus to edit its name/abbreviation. Bus routing is saved per audio device.
If an output is greyed out it may be in use by SMPTE: change the SMPTE routing or disable SMPTE output in General settings.

Download a song: when adding a song, tap Add in the top-right corner. In the Setlists menu, tap Open Setlist, select a setlist, and tap the download icons to download tracks without loading the setlist, or load it to download every song automatically. Songs already on the device from another setlist show no download icon.

Remove one setlist from the device: open it in the Setlists menu and choose Remove Setlist From Device. Remove all: Setlists menu > Delete All Setlists From Device. This does not delete setlists from your MultiTracks.com account; re-download from the setlist menu to recover.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: Subscription not recognized: Settings > About > Restore Purchases. The guide says: if an iTunes subscription is expired or not being confirmed by Playback, reconcile any payment issues in the App Store and tap Restore Purchases to reconnect your In-App Subscription.
steps.caution: Updating the app closes Playback and takes a few minutes; don't do this during a service.

steps.text: Side menu (stack icon) shows user name, organization name and ID, Switch Organizations, and Log Out.
steps.caution: Signing out can interrupt cloud access until you sign back in.

results.title: Troubleshooting Playback Download Errors
results.summary: Covers four named download error messages in Playback (Error Authorizing, Audio Files Missing, Insufficient Storage, generic Download Error) plus a catch-all. MultiTracks says download errors are rare and asks users who see the same error repeatedly to report it through the website chat. The article does not name a platform; it refers only to 'the device' and 'the Playback app'. Each step belongs to its named-error section. The remove/re-add and alternate-key quick fixes are documented under generic Download Error; that section does not establish them as Audio Files Missing recovery.

steps.text: 'Error Authorizing': the download failed a security check (your network may be blocking Playback from verifying the device). Follow the separate article 'Playback Download Error (Download Unauthorized)'.
'Audio Files Missing': tap Try Again at least three times. On the third attempt Playback runs a different recovery routine automatically.

'Audio Files Missing' (if three attempts fail on a song you recently downloaded in past setlists): open the setlist menu, scroll to the bottom, and select 'Delete All Setlists from Device'. Last resort only: it removes all local downloads and every current setlist must be downloaded again.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: 'Insufficient Storage': remove past setlists with 'Delete all setlists from device' at the bottom of the setlist menu. If the error persists, check the device's storage; it may be too full. A typical song is roughly 40 MB to 1 GB, so a full setlist can be several GB.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: 'Download Error' (generic): tap Try Again at least two times. If it continues and you are short on time, use Contact Support in the About tab of Playback Settings, then try the quick fixes.

'Download Error' (generic section, after retries and contacting support) - Quick fix 1 - remove and re-add the song: tap Edit, tap the red minus icon on the song, tap '+ Add Song', find the song again, and load it.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: 'Download Error' (generic section, after retries and contacting support) - Quick fix 2 - download in another key and transpose locally: before loading, change the song's key in song settings to a key close to the one you need; after the download, open song settings in edit mode and change the key back.

'Download Error' (generic section, after retries and contacting support) - Quick fix 3 - clear local data (last resort): contact support first from the About tab, then open the setlist menu (top-right) and select 'Delete All Setlists from Device' at the bottom. All setlists must be redownloaded afterward.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: Any other error: contact MultiTracks.com through the website messenger or 'Contact Support' in the About tab of the Playback app.

results.title: Playback Subscriptions | Explained
results.summary: Separates Playback Features (Intro, Premium, Cloud Pro, Live Bundle), Playback Content (Rentals, purchased tracks, Sounds, uploaded Cloud Songs, click and guide), and Playback Access (Team Sharing seats). Playback Intro is free on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS but limited to a single stereo output and excludes Premium features (editing arrangements, Playback Remote, Playback Sync). Cloud Pro adds click and guide for every song, Team Sharing seats, and saved custom-named arrangements; uploading Cloud Songs requires Cloud Pro. Rentals are device-specific and not shared. The article does not explain how to check or manage the subscription in-app.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > App Overview > Login Requirements > Organizational Content Permissions
results.text:
If you are logging into your own organization, then you are ready to start downloading your organization’s purchased content or Rental credits immediately. When logging into another organization, certain permission subscriptions need to be added to your account in order for you to access purchased tracks, spend Rental credits, or save Cloud changes to setlists, song arrangements, and MIDI Cues.

For more information about managing your organization’s team members, subscriptions, and content permissions, check out: 📖 Managing Roles and Permissions

Once logged in, you’re ready to start building a setlist!

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > App Overview > Login Requirements > Organizations vs. Users
results.text: An organization in the MultiTracks.com ecosystem is the umbrella under which content can be purchased, users can be added, and subscriptions can be shared. When an 'account' is created using the "Sign Up" flow, an organization and a user is created simultaneously and the user is set as the owner of the organization. When logging into Playback, there is an organization selection prompt, to select which organization to log into. If you are a user belonging only to the organization created when you built your account, then select that organization. However, a user can be added to other existing MultiTracks.com organizations and have access to content belonging to those organizations in Playback. Every organization that you've been added to will be available at this login screen.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Building a Setlist > Adding A Song in Playback > Options in the Add a Song menu
results.text:
- 1) Search
   This quick search option will filter through every single song in the MultiTracks.com catalog and your organization’s Library of purchased songs and uploaded Cloud songs.
- 2) All Songs
   Discover new songs in the MultiTracks.com catalog. Search by New Releases, Top Songs, and more.
  - Why don't I see this? The All Songs catalog in Playback is available for users with a Playback Rentals subscription or a Cloud Pro subscription.
     ​Note: If your organization has a Cloud Pro subscription or Playback Rentals, the Click and Guide of any catalog song can be added to your setlist without tracks.
- 3) Library
   Every song with any purchased content, active rentals, and Cloud Songs are all included in your Library. Sort by songs, artists, themes, and more.
- 4) Click & Pad
   Add a Click & Pad to your setlist for creating extended moments. Give it a name, assign an ambient pad for the Pad Player to play, and determine the tempo/time signature of the click track.
